mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in housing starts, as measured by HOUST, indicates a growing demand for housing and related goods, which in turn drives economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong housing starts growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of high federal funds rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate, as measured by UNRATE, indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to decreased consumer spending and ultimately result in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in high unemployment periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production, as measured by INDPRO, indicates a growing supply of goods, which can lead to increased economic activity and ultimately result in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong industrial production growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in retail sales, as measured by RSAFS, and a corresponding increase in housing starts, as measured by HOUST, indicate a growing demand for goods and services, which in turn drives economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong retail sales and housing starts growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate, as measured by FEDFUNDS, and a corresponding increase in the consumer price index, as measured by CPIAUCSL, indicate an expansionary monetary policy, which can lead to increased borrowing and spending, and ultimately result in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3.5% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of low federal funds rates and high consumer price index growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate, as measured by UNRATE, and a corresponding increase in payroll employment, as measured by PAYEMS, indicate a strengthening labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and ultimately result in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls < 4.5% and PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in low unemployment and high payroll employment periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the GDP, as measured by GDPC1, indicates a slowing economy, which can lead to decreased economic activity and ultimately result in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of slow GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).
